column8: CFPB giving cover to EWA industry while courts disagree. Resolution uncertain.

column6: Individual provider action but signals regulatory attention to cash advance apps.

column6: If passed, first state-level BNPL regulatory framework. Model for others.
column8: State action filling federal vacuum. But single-state rules have limited market impact.

column5: 8 federal courts ruled that EWA "tips," donations, expedite fees ARE finance charges under TILA.
column6: EWA apps may need to comply with lending regulations, disclose APRs.
column8: Courts contradicting CFPB. If lending classification sticks, entire EWA model may break.

column5: FICO 10 BNPL and FICO 10 T BNPL scores launching Fall 2025. First credit scores incorporating BNPL data.
column6: If adopted by lenders, would partially close visibility gap. But requires BNPL reporting.
column8: Adoption is key question. Most BNPL providers still don't report. Score without data = useless.

column5: Colorado EWA licensing law (HB25-1020) LIVE Jan 1 2026. Providers must be licensed; fee cap $5 per advance (<$75) or $7 per advance (>$75); at least one no-cost option required; no credit reporting; no late fees.
column6: State-level EWA regulation now enforceable. Effectively caps fees for Colorado consumers.
column8: Fourth state with comprehensive EWA licensing. Accelerating state-by-state patchwork. CFPB gap being filled.

column5: Connecticut enacted EWA law (effective Oct 1 2025). Caps finance charges at $4 per advance or $30 per month. Treats EWA fees as finance charges — aligned with courts, not CFPB advisory.
column6: Model law classifying EWA as loan product with finance charge caps. Sets precedent.
column8: Connecticut joined California in loan classification. 12 states now have EWA laws, ~20 considering. State wave accelerating as CFPB retreats.

column5: CFPB chief legal officer Mark Paoletta filed motion to WITHDRAW Rule 1033 from litigation. CFPB calling own rule unlawful and arguing it should be set aside entirely.
column6: Rule 1033 now effectively dead — not just enjoined but being actively withdrawn by agency.
column8: Visibility shock will NOT come via regulation. Phantom debt stays invisible until defaults spike. Escalates from ON_HOLD → DEAD. Prediction PHAN-P03 confidence: 75%→90%.
